summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease, and type 2 diabetes was admitted due to elevated liver enzymes concerning for transplant rejection. Initial ultrasound showed patent hepatic vasculature, coarsened liver texture, and moderate ascites. A liver biopsy confirmed acute cellular rejection, prompting treatment with IV methylprednisolone, increased tacrolimus, and initiation of mycophenolate mofetil. A second biopsy showed improvement. During admission, she developed steroid-induced hyperglycemia requiring insulin therapy, and a urinary tract infection with Klebsiella pneumoniae and Citrobacter koseri was treated. Her kidney function declined (creatinine up to 1.8), leading to holding of Lasix. She underwent therapeutic paracentesis for symptomatic ascites, which was sterile. She was transitioned to oral prednisone, carvedilol for blood pressure and variceal prophylaxis, and discharged home with close follow-up for tacrolimus monitoring and steroid tapering.
